title: Add proof contracts for delivery workflows
body:
## Motivation

A workflow can pass a valid boundary case—for example, producing no invented
output for empty or ambient input—without demonstrating the primary promise
that representative input produces the expected user-visible result. If both
are treated as interchangeable command successes, a run can finish green while
the promised capability remains unproven.

Tractor cannot infer product truth from fixture names, diagrams, or tests. This
PR instead lets a project declare that truth as a compact, machine-checkable
proof contract before implementation.

## Design

- Adds explicit top-level workflow intent: `mode: delivery` or
  `mode: discovery`.
- Delivery requires a `proof_contract` declaring the primary outcome,
  qualifying primary cases, expected observable outputs, correctness oracles,
  evidence source/surface and independence, boundary cases, required
  capabilities, unknowns, scope gaps, and terminal coverage.
- Discovery may remain contract-light and terminates as
  `LEARNING_COMPLETED`, not delivered product success.
- Generated schema, semantic lint, CLI/MCP help, examples, and authoring docs
  expose the same model.
- The minimized runtime provenance record keeps only run/case/node/execution
  identity, the successful route, a digest binding the case and exact tool
  declaration, ordered snapshot digests, and hashes of engine-owned
  `outcome.json` and `tool.log`. Roles, architecture-edge labels, capture
  timing, and snapshot paths are derived from the digested declaration rather
  than duplicated in checkpoint state.

## Terminal enforcement

For delivery, Tractor records proof only when a distinct top-level tool case
uses independent current-run evidence and follows its exit-zero `on_success`
route. Before returning `COMPLETED`, the engine verifies every required primary
and boundary case, the current run ID, assertion mapping and success route,
the current case/tool digest, deterministic before/after snapshots, and the
engine outcome/log hashes. Material scope gaps also block completion.

A boundary pass cannot satisfy a missing primary case. Missing, substituted,
or changed evidence leaves the run non-terminal and preserves a retry
continuation. Existing nonzero tool behavior is unchanged: `on_error` still
routes to the authored fix path and creates no proof pass.

## Compatibility

Workflow mode is optional as a legacy compatibility path. Existing graphs that
omit it preserve their previous validation and `COMPLETED` behavior and do not
need a proof contract. New or materially edited delivery workflows can opt in
explicitly; discovery consumers should recognize `LEARNING_COMPLETED` as
terminal learning rather than product delivery.

This is an unreleased checkpoint extension, so there is no released proof-state
migration. A checkpoint produced by an intermediate version of this branch
should rerun its proof under the final compact representation.

## Scope and non-goals

Tractor enforces declared contracts; it does not determine whether a fixture
really qualifies, whether an oracle is product-correct, or whether an
`operating_layer` command truly reaches the claimed surface. Local evidence is
auditable, not a cryptographically trusted remote attestation. Artifact capture
currently copies whole regular files, and automated proof cases are restricted
to top-level tool nodes.

The implementation is domain-neutral and adds no dependency on external local
skills, Codex task/thread concepts, or Codex-specific proof machinery.

## Validation

- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go tool goimports -d` on changed Go files
- `go tool modernize ./engine ./examples`
- `go generate ./graph` with no generated drift
- `tractor validate` for both proof-readiness examples
- targeted `vp check --no-lint` for changed formatter-managed docs
- `format:rsvelte:check`, `lint:rsvelte`, `check:rsvelte`, and `check:astro`
- static site build and preview verification (3 routes, 4 Pages-safe assets)

The aggregate `pnpm verify` stops at its first formatter gate: the restored
upstream layout of `skills/tractor/SKILL.md` and unchanged
`src/content/docs/loops.md` differ from the current formatter. Targeted changed
docs and all subsequent checks pass. `golangci-lint` was not rerun on the final
tree because no local executable was installed and external acquisition was
unavailable; the final tree did pass the race suite, vet, and modernize checks
listed above.

## Suggested review order

1. [Promise-to-Proof design and limits](https://github.com/skundalkar/tractor/blob/codex/proof-readiness-contract/docs/proof-readiness.md)
2. [Normative workflow and checkpoint semantics](https://github.com/skundalkar/tractor/blob/codex/proof-readiness-contract/docs/spec.md)
3. [Example overview](https://github.com/skundalkar/tractor/blob/codex/proof-readiness-contract/examples/proof-readiness/README.md)
4. [Delivery example with required primary and boundary cases](https://github.com/skundalkar/tractor/blob/codex/proof-readiness-contract/examples/proof-readiness/required-happy-path.yaml)
5. [Contract-light discovery example](https://github.com/skundalkar/tractor/blob/codex/proof-readiness-contract/examples/proof-readiness/discovery.yaml)

title: codergen agent writes declared artifact to pipeline workdir instead of branch worktree; collection fails whole run
body:
## Summary

A `codergen` branch agent wrote its declared artifact to the **pipeline workdir root** instead of its assigned branch worktree. Artifact collection `lstat`s only the worktree path, so the whole run FAILED at fan-out collection — even though the stage itself completed successfully (its `outcome.json` says "Wrote findings to claude_critique.md") and the other two branches had valid artifacts in place.

Observed on tractor MCP plugin 0.7.1, run via Claude Code.

## Repro / evidence

Pipeline: 3-branch `parallel` critique + `parallel.fan_in` (same shape as a working prior run), branch artifact declared as `artifacts: [claude_critique.md]`, provider `anthropic`/`claude-sonnet-5`, `fidelity: none`.

- Stage `resolved.json` shows the correct worktree workdir:
  `workdir: .../.tractor/runs/56f09868.../worktrees-1248417954/branch-001`
- Failure:
  `pipeline failed: collect artifact "claude_critique.md" for branch "claude_critique": lstat .../worktrees-1248417954/branch-001/claude_critique.md: no such file or directory`
- The file was found afterwards at the **pipeline workdir root** (`<repo>/claude_critique.md`), fully written.
- Branches 002 (codex) and 003 (gemini) wrote their artifacts into their worktrees correctly on the same run.

## Likely mechanism

The node prompt names the artifact as a bare filename ("Record material findings … in claude_critique.md") while the goal text necessarily references repo-relative paths (`docs/research/...`). The agent apparently resolved an absolute path to the main repo (discoverable from the worktree's gitdir metadata and prompt context) and wrote there. Nothing in the harness (a) re-anchors artifact paths to the stage workdir in the delivered prompt, (b) detects out-of-worktree writes, or (c) looks anywhere but the worktree at collection time.

## Impact

- One branch's path confusion fails the entire run at collection, after all branch spend.
- Stage outcome says success while the run says FAILED — the mismatch only surfaces at collect time, with no pointer to the stray file.

## Workaround that worked

`mv <repo>/claude_critique.md <worktree>/claude_critique.md`, then `start_run` with `resume: true` on the same `logs_root` — resumed cleanly past collection.

## Suggested fixes (any subset)

1. **Collection fallback + diagnostics**: on missing artifact, scan the pipeline workdir (and any CWD the agent CLI reported) for the exact artifact basename; either collect-with-warning or fail with a message naming the stray location and the one-line `mv` + `resume` fix.
2. **Prompt hardening**: harness appends an explicit line to codergen prompts: "Write declared artifacts relative to your working directory: `<abs worktree path>`."
3. **Containment tripwire**: after a codergen stage, flag writes that landed outside the assigned worktree (the pipeline workdir was a git repo here, so it showed up as an untracked file in the *user's* repo — worth preventing on principle).
4. **Branch-scoped retry**: let a collection failure retry/fail just that branch instead of the run (resume handled this well, but only after manual file surgery).

## Environment

- tractor plugin 0.7.1 (MCP), macOS (darwin 25.5.0)
- Run id `56f09868b664afced18fc5e67cd1638b`; resumed as `5e7ce7bc95de86fc4b5bc0db62128cdd`
- Unrelated observation in the same run's stderr, separate issue if interesting: codex branch logged `apply_patch verification failed: invalid patch: multiple operations target ~/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md` (did not affect its artifact).

title: Codex adapter: spawns a fresh app-server subprocess per session instead of reusing the local daemon
body:
## Summary

\`harness/codex/rpc.go\`'s \`defaultProcessConfig()\` always spawns a brand-new \`codex app-server --stdio\` child process per \`CreateSession\` call:

```go
func defaultProcessConfig() processConfig {
	return processConfig{
		command: "codex",
		args:    []string{"app-server", "--stdio"},
		env:     os.Environ(),
	}
}
```

The \`codex\` CLI already ships a supported persistent-daemon path we're not using:

- \`codex app-server daemon start\` — starts a local daemon if one isn't already running, with a control socket at \`~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock\`.
- \`codex app-server proxy --sock <path>\` — proxies stdio to that running daemon instead of spawning a new app-server process.

Switching the adapter to attach to the daemon instead of spawning its own subprocess would avoid paying app-server startup cost on every session.

## Related open question: GUI visibility

Threads created via \`thread/start\` (regardless of which process created them — our own subprocess, the daemon, or ChatGPT.app's embedded instance) are written to the same on-disk store under \`~/.codex/sessions/\`, which ChatGPT Desktop's history reads from. So Tractor-driven Codex sessions currently show up in ChatGPT Desktop's session list (see [openai/codex#16614](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16614) — third-party app-server clients' threads appear there, mistagged as \`source: "vscode"\`).

Switching to the daemon path (above) does **not** by itself fix this, since it's the same shared thread store either way. The old \`attractor\` reference client used \`ephemeral: true\` on \`thread/start\` for scratch/throwaway sessions, but ephemeral threads don't appear to get a durable, resumable rollout — which conflicts with Tractor's need to resume sessions across turns. Whether there's a way to keep a thread both durable/resumable *and* hidden from ChatGPT Desktop's history is unresolved and needs its own investigation.

## Suggested next steps

1. Point the adapter at \`codex app-server daemon\` + \`proxy --sock\` instead of spawning its own \`--stdio\` subprocess per session.
2. Separately investigate whether any \`thread/start\` metadata can keep a durable/resumable thread out of ChatGPT Desktop's session list.

title: Expose normalized usage and quota telemetry
body:
## Problem

Tractor preserves native harness events but cannot answer typed questions about token burn, cached input, context-window pressure, cost, or provider quota reset windows. That limits operator visibility and blocks the north star's reserved path toward usage-aware higher-order routing.

The archived Attractor backend normalized stable usage fields and decoded Codex five-hour and weekly rate-limit windows.

## Request

Add a provider-neutral usage snapshot that adapters populate when native data is available, aggregate it into run status, and preserve the provider-native event or payload for fields outside the common model.

This issue is telemetry only. It must not add usage-aware routing policy yet.

## Acceptance criteria

- The common model covers input, output, cached-input, and total tokens; context-window size or utilization; cost when reported; and named quota windows with usage and reset time.
- Codex maps app-server token and rate-limit notifications into the common model.
- Claude maps only fields the native harness actually reports and leaves unavailable fields absent.
- Per-turn data is aggregated without double-counting cumulative provider snapshots.
- Run logs and MCP status expose the latest typed snapshot and run aggregate.
- Raw native observations remain available for audit and forward compatibility.
- Missing telemetry never changes run success or failure.
- Tests cover mapping, absent fields, cumulative-vs-delta accounting, quota windows, persistence, and resume.

## Source references

Archived provider-neutral usage contract:
https://github.com/tylergannon/attractor/blob/0aca8b748e6ecc23446fc690d2b66690b77fe0d3/harness_backend.go

Archived Codex quota decoding:
https://github.com/tylergannon/attractor/blob/0aca8b748e6ecc23446fc690d2b66690b77fe0d3/internal/codexapp/client.go#L602

title: Use one sortable run ID end to end
body:
## Problem

Tractor currently uses a random hexadecimal manifest ID while run directories and MCP state have separate allocation or ordering conventions. Runs are harder to correlate by eye, sort chronologically, and carry consistently across CLI output, manifests, logs, control paths, and MCP state.

The archived Attractor CLI used lowercase ULIDs.

## Request

Allocate one opaque, lowercase, time-sortable run ID for every new run and use it end to end.

The identifier should be created once, then propagated rather than independently reconstructed by the manifest, directory allocator, or MCP layer. Existing persisted run IDs should remain readable as opaque identifiers; new compatibility machinery is not required.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every new run receives one lowercase sortable ID with sufficient collision resistance.
- The same ID appears in the run directory, manifest, CLI output, and MCP persisted state/status.
- Lexical order matches creation order at the allocator's timestamp precision.
- Callers may still supply an explicit valid run ID where the existing API permits it.
- Resume and control operations treat IDs as opaque and continue to open existing runs.
- Tests fix time and entropy to verify shape, ordering, propagation, collision handling, and existing-run lookup.
- Documentation identifies the run ID as the canonical correlation key.

## Source reference

Archived Attractor ULID allocation at 0aca8b7:
https://github.com/tylergannon/attractor/blob/0aca8b748e6ecc23446fc690d2b66690b77fe0d3/cmd/attractor/main.go#L589

title: Generate the complete Codex app-server wire protocol
body:
## Problem

Tractor runs codex app-server generate-json-schema but generates Go code only for TurnStartParams. JSON-RPC envelopes, errors, notifications, and observed response shapes in harness/codex/rpc.go and adapter code remain handwritten.

That is not an all-generated wire contract. It allows Codex protocol drift to become a runtime failure, makes coverage difficult to audit, and hides new app-server capabilities until someone manually models them. The original Tractor design explicitly chose this narrow generation; this request supersedes that choice.

## Request

Check in the complete current Codex app-server JSON Schema snapshot, generate Go models for the full protocol, and replace all handwritten structs that mirror app-server wire types with generated types.

Handwritten code should own transport and behavior only: process lifecycle, request correlation, dispatch, adapter semantics, and error categorization. It should not redefine protocol shapes.

## Acceptance criteria

- The complete app-server schema output used by Tractor is checked in at a named Codex CLI version.
- A deterministic generation command produces all Go wire models Tractor needs from that complete snapshot.
- JSON-RPC requests, responses, notifications, errors, IDs, and method-specific params/results consumed by Tractor use generated types.
- Handwritten mirror structs such as rpcMessage and rpcError are removed.
- Unknown future notifications remain safely ignorable without weakening typed handling of known messages.
- Generation either handles shared definitions and unsupported schema constructs deterministically or fails with a clear actionable error; no manual edits to generated files are required.
- A clean-tree drift check proves regeneration is reproducible.
- Adapter tests cover typed dispatch, provider errors, malformed messages, and at least one real app-server smoke flow through the generated surface.
- The supported Codex protocol/schema version and refresh procedure are documented.

## Source references

Tractor's current narrow generator:
https://github.com/tylergannon/tractor/blob/main/harness/codex/schema/generate.go

Archived complete protocol snapshot and generated types:
https://github.com/tylergannon/attractor/tree/0aca8b748e6ecc23446fc690d2b66690b77fe0d3/internal/codexapp/schema

title: Add stable model aliases
body:
## Problem

Pipeline definitions currently embed provider-native model IDs or depend on entry-point defaults. That makes graphs noisy, turns every graph into its own model-version policy, and makes a coordinated model upgrade require edits across authored workflows.

The archived Attractor implementation isolated this concern in a small alias resolver while continuing to accept raw model IDs.

## Request

Add a repo-owned model alias registry used consistently by graph execution, the CLI, and MCP-started runs.

Raw provider-native IDs must remain a supported escape hatch. Alias resolution should return both provider and concrete model, reject an explicitly conflicting provider, and fail clearly for a known alias that is temporarily unsupported.

## Acceptance criteria

- A small documented set of aliases resolves to provider plus concrete model.
- Graph, CLI, and MCP execution use the same resolver.
- Raw model IDs continue to work without registration.
- An explicit provider that conflicts with an alias is rejected before harness activity.
- Unknown aliases are not silently rewritten.
- Tests cover resolution, raw IDs, conflicts, unsupported aliases, and entry-point consistency.
- User-facing documentation explains that aliases are maintained policy and raw IDs are the stability escape hatch.

## Source reference

Archived Attractor resolver at 0aca8b7:
https://github.com/tylergannon/attractor/blob/0aca8b748e6ecc23446fc690d2b66690b77fe0d3/internal/modelalias/modelalias.go
